#### **Course Outline**

Welcome to the **living Introduction to Statistics in Health and Social Care playbook**.
This playbook is designed to interlace with the content on the Learn pages and follow the same weekly structure (chapters) and topics within weeks (sections).

This course serves not only as an introduction to the statistical theory side, but importantly how to implement this in a data-science context.
To that extent, you should ensure you are ready to implement all concepts in R.
Throughout, you will find model code (grey boxes), such as the block below.
The below ensures you have all the relevant packages for this course installed and it is recommended that you run it to avoid later issues.

```{r}
# Install the tidyverse package, which includes dplyr, ggplot2, and other useful packages
install.packages("tidyverse")

# Load the tidyverse package
library(tidyverse)
```

The ‘tidyverse‘ package is a collection of R packages that includes:

-   dplyr: For data manipulation.
-   ggplot2: For data visualisation.
-   readr: For reading data.
-   purrr: For functional programming.
-   tibble: For creating tidy data frames.
-   stringr: For string manipulation.
-   forcats: For working with factors.

Throughout you will also see boxes which are in yellow.
Similarly these are also R code, except they follow content which is analogous to that presented in weekly slides, or in the self-guided lab or code-along.
This to help you see how the content all pieces together.
An example of a yellow code block is presented below:

::: analogous code
<details>

```{r}
# Calculating Z-scores for the "pain_score" variable in the licorice_gargle dataset

licorice_gargle <- licorice_gargle %>%
mutate(z_score_pain = (pain_score - mean(pain_score, na.rm = TRUE)) /
sd(pain_score, na.rm = TRUE))

# Print the updated data with Z-scores
print(licorice_gargle)
```

</details>
:::

## Course learning outcomes

On successful completion of this course, you should be able to:

1.Demonstrate a critical understanding of the fundamental concepts of statistics.
2.Apply basic statistical techniques using the statistical software R to solve simple problems from health, social and care settings.
3.Analyse and interpret data from health and social care, using appropriate statistical tests 4.Demonstrate the ability to effectively communicate basic statistical techniques with peers and a wide range of audiences within the health and social care sector.
